answer:
Based on the spatial analysis performed, I joined the 256 incidents to the 9 zones (251 matched; 5 fell outside all zone boundaries and were excluded) and computed incident rates per 1,000 residents for each zone.

**Zone Z2 has the highest incident rate at 22.89 incidents per 1,000 residents.** This is driven by its small population (830 residents) relative to its incident count (19 incidents). For comparison, the next-highest rate is Z5 at 8.92 per 1,000 — Z2's rate is roughly 2.6× higher than the second-place zone.

Here are the full results:

| Zone | Population | Incidents | Rate per 1,000 |
|------|-----------:|----------:|---------------:|
| Z1 | 5,200 | 41 | 7.88 |
| **Z2** | **830** | **19** | **22.89** |
| Z3 | 4,100 | 22 | 5.37 |
| Z4 | 2,600 | 18 | 6.92 |
| Z5 | 7,400 | 66 | 8.92 |
| Z6 | 3,900 | 25 | 6.41 |
| Z7 | 1,500 | 9 | 6.00 |
| Z8 | 6,100 | 37 | 6.07 |
| Z9 | 2,800 | 14 | 5.00 |

**Artifacts produced:**
- **Interactive choropleth map** of incidents per zone: [incidents_per_zone.geojson](https://agent/files/file_e399948e89fb/download) (on your map, shaded by `point_count`)
- **Per-zone table CSV**: [incidents_per_zone_table.csv](https://agent/files/file_089288213e85/download)
- **Full results with rates**: [incident_rates_per_zone.csv](https://agent/files/file_6ef187ba9336/download)

Note: 5 of the 256 incidents (≈2%) fell outside all 9 zone polygons and were excluded from the counts.
